title: Nearly 1,400 Workers Laid Off at Ohio Truck Factory
summary:
Nearly 1,400 people lost their jobs at what had been the Navistar truck factory in Springfield, Ohio. The layoffs happened on Wednesday, three days before President Donald Trump's planned rally at a nearby high school. A layoff means a worker loses a job because an employer cuts jobs.

The job losses were roughly equal to a whole year of job growth in the greater Dayton area. Kyle Bos was one of the workers. He has two daughters, with a third due in January. He said rising grocery prices were also making life harder for his family.

Bos belongs to the United Auto Workers union. He said he had voted for Trump three times. Now he plans to help Democrats win votes before the November election. He said the layoffs were one reason for that change.

The Dayton area has lost about half of its 90,000 factory jobs since 1990, according to federal data. In recent years, its economy has improved as Wright-Patterson Air Force Base expanded. The base directly employs 38,000 people. Its innovations have also attracted aircraft companies to the area.

Trump said manufacturing was coming back. The White House pointed to an $850 million investment by aircraft maker Electra as evidence that his policies were creating jobs.

Jeff Hoagland, CEO of the Dayton Development Coalition, said both Republicans and Democrats had recognized the base's value. He explained that developing an economy takes time.
why_it_matters: Job losses affect families' income and can influence what voters want from elected leaders.
